scenes.headline: How a Mac runs a model that does not fit
scenes.sub: Experts on disk, a shared pool of slots in memory
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jackstay! This engine runs a huge model on a Mac that cannot hold it.

scenes.text: Most of the model is experts, and each token uses few. Keep the busy ones in a shared pool of slots, and read the rest from disk.
scenes.say: Most of the model is experts, and a token needs only a few. The busy ones stay in a pool of slots, and the rest wait on disk.

steps.say: Each layer, the router picks ten of five hundred twelve experts and looks for each in the pool.
An expert already in a slot goes straight to the graphics chip, which gathers it by slot number.
A missing one is read from disk into a slot, about three megabytes, with no cache in between.
A forecast runs the router of a later layer early, so some reads finish before they are asked for.

scenes.title: Which slot gets reused
scenes.say: The pool is shared by every layer, and one simple scan chooses what to evict.

items.say: A hit marks the slot as recently used.
A miss sweeps a hand around the pool.
It skips the slots this layer is still using.
The first unmarked slot is the one that gets replaced.

scenes.title: How often the pool already had it
scenes.note: 156 experts a layer, from the project's own receipts
scenes.say: In the project's own runs, the pool already held the expert eighty to ninety six percent of the time.

scenes.label: needed if nothing were cached
scenes.say: With an empty cache the disk would have to deliver almost thirty gigabytes a second. It tops out near seventeen.

scenes.text: It is a caching problem: the pool hits 80 to 96% of lookups, and disk waits take 11 to 30%.
scenes.say: So the speed is a caching problem. Most lookups hit, and the disk wait is a minor part of each token.

recap: A shared pool of slots caches them.
scenes.say: Experts on disk, a shared pool in memory, and a forecast to hide the reads.
